Hablemos de Bad Bunny!

Who is Bad Bunny?

Bad Bunny (born Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio in 1994) is a Puerto Rican singer, rapper, and songwriter known for his influence on Latin trap and reggaeton. He gained international fame with his unique blend of reggaeton, Latin trap, and other genres, often incorporating socially conscious themes into his music. His breakthrough came with hits like Soy Peor, Mía (feat. Drake), and I Like It (with Cardi B and J Balvin). He has since released multiple chart-topping albums, including YHLQMDLG, El Último Tour Del Mundo, and Un Verano Sin Ti, and most recently Debí Tirar Más Fotos, solidifying his status as one of the most influential Latin artists globally

Data Analysis

Data Source

I extracted the data using the spotifyr package, and stored it in the data folder.

Import Data

# install.packages("ggplot2")
# install.packages("dplyr")
# install.packages("knitr")
# Packages needed for analysing the data
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(tidyverse)
# Import data into df

# df <- read.csv("data/BBunny.csv")
df <- read.csv("data/BBunny.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)

Data Preparation

I have removed all duplicates and albums that Bad Bunny featured in but are not his own albums in my data frame and also removed the live versions of the same songs.

#filter out albums that Bad Bunny only featured in but are not his own (only albums published before 2022 contained in dataset so I am only filtering those out)
BB_original <- c("Un Verano Sin Ti", "EL ÚLTIMO TOUR DEL MUNDO", "LAS QUE NO IBAN A SALIR", "YHLQMDLG", "OASIS", "X 100PRE")

df <- df |> filter(album_name %in% BB_original)

# remove all duplicate tracks
df <- df |> distinct(track_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Filter out track names that include "Live at" or "Live Acoustic"
df <- df |> filter(!grepl("Live at|Live Acoustic", track_name))
# Change the data type of album_name from numeric into character
df$album_name <- as.character(df$album_name)

Album Analysis (Valence & Popularity)

Valence

# Change album_name from character to factor before plotting
df$album_name <- as.factor(df$album_name)

# Order the albums based on release year (from latest release to earlier ones)
album_order <- c("Un Verano Sin Ti", "EL ÚLTIMO TOUR DEL MUNDO", "LAS QUE NO IBAN A SALIR", "YHLQMDLG", "OASIS", "X 100PRE")
# Convert album_name into a factor with specified order
df$album_name <- factor(df$album_name, levels = album_order)

# Plot a boxplot
ggplot(df, aes(x=album_name, y=valence))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album Name", y="Valence")
  # theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  
  # Rotates x-axis labels for readability

The valence level of the albums fluctuates quite a bit over the different albums but 2 main clusters: positive albums with high valence (OASIS & YHLQMDLG) and lower valence overall more negative albums (Un Verano Sin Ti, EL ÚLTIMO TOUR DEL MUNDO, X 100PRE).

Nonetheless, the distribution of valence data under each album generally seems to be quite skewed.

Popularity

ggplot(df, aes(x=album_name, y=popularity))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album name", y="Popularity")

Bad Bunny’s later-released albums seem to be more popular, which trend probably reflects the increased fame and fans acquired as his music career gained more and more traction over the years.
